name: The Millennials Kyoto
detail: I was very satisfied :) First of all, the bedding was really comfortable, and since there were blinds installed, even though it was a dormitory, I could rest comfortably like in a private room. The amenities were also conveniently prepared in various ways. Towels, slippers, toothbrushes, toothpaste, razors, earplugs, shampoo, conditioner, body wash, etc. were available at the front, so I could take as much as I needed and use them comfortably. The shower and restroom were divided into several stalls, so there was almost no waiting while using them. All the staff were friendly, and the lounge had a water dispenser, ice maker, coffee machine, refrigerator, and kitchen facilities, so it was great to be able to prepare simple food myself. The refrigerator was set up so that I could store my items by writing the checkout date, room number, and name, which was convenient. Above all, the location was really good! Not only were there convenience facilities, but the subway and bus stops were also nearby, making it easy to explore Kyoto and come back late. During my stay, all the guests were quiet and respectful, which made for a more comfortable experience. Overall, it was a very satisfying stay. I would love to try other locations as well, not just in Kyoto! 😊

name: GLANSIT KYOTO KAWARAMACHI
detail: All floors have shower rooms available. Each floor has one shower room with a bathtub. The staff are friendly, the facilities are clean, and transport is convenient as the subway and bus are close by, with the market and riverside right in front. A 24 or 25-inch suitcase fits in the locker. You can come back after exploring a place in the morning and take a rest. Many places have restrictions on access during cleaning times for long stays, but there were no such limitations at Glanjit, which was nice. There are water dispensers and microwaves on every floor, and there are vending machines for drinks on the first floor. They provide one large towel and one small towel each day, so there was no shortage. Amenities are available on the first floor, so you can just take what you need. I felt that the staff and the system cared a lot about how it would be for travelers. Thanks to that, I had a great stay in Kyoto.

name: Livemax Hostels Kyoto Ekimae
detail: An experience that exceeded expectations. The hotel is located near Kyoto Station, making it very convenient to access popular attractions in Kyoto through the station, and there are many convenience stores and restaurants nearby, which makes life convenient. The room is very clean, and the bed space is larger than expected, quite spacious for a single bed. The air in the room is good, without any strange odors, and other guests are well-mannered, all trying to keep the noise down. The shared restrooms and showers are also clean, and there is no need to wait in line.

name: Almont Hotel Kyoto
detail: The characteristic of Japanese hotels is that if you spread out two suitcases, it's all done, but this place was completely different. The room was spacious enough even with two beds, and I loved the pretty lighting. The bathroom and shower area were separate, and with a bathtub included, there was plenty of space, making me very satisfied. The front desk service was perfect, and they understood everything perfectly when I spoke in English, so there was no problem with communication. I also made good use of the luggage storage available before and after check-in. Although it's said to be far from Kyoto Station, I didn't feel any inconvenience because the alleyways were well arranged. I will definitely use this place again when I visit Kyoto next time!

name: Hotel Elcient Kyoto Hachijoguchi
detail: As soon as I entered the facility, there was a pleasant fragrance, it was clean, and there were plenty of chairs at the front desk. I was satisfied that I could store my luggage both after check-in and after check-out. The amenities were mostly well-prepared, and I was happy that they were also available in the bathroom. The large public bath was spacious and clean, and there were various types of shampoo available, which made me satisfied. The breakfast had a wide variety of food typical of Kyoto, including desserts, and I was happy with it. There was nothing disappointing about this affordable and excellent hotel, and I definitely want to use it again next time. If I had to mention something, it was that since I was on the fifth floor, the view wasn't great.

name: RIHGA Royal Hotel Kyoto
detail: I went by motorcycle this time. The motorcycle parking was a bit tight, but the staff at the entrance were very kind. Thank you. The front desk staff who checked us in seemed a bit nervous but I thought they were doing their best. It's a short walk to Kyoto Station, but there's also a shuttle bus available. Everything here feels like a luxury hotel. There are boutiques, restaurants, and a bar inside the hotel. The property is spacious, so taxis and private cars come and go frequently, and the staff are quick and efficient, leaving a very good impression. The room was spacious enough to move around comfortably. The television was located in the corner of the room, which made it a bit difficult to see. The washroom was clean, and the bath was spacious and comfortable. The softness of the pillows is a matter of personal preference. Due to budget constraints, I didn’t include breakfast, but this hotel has made me want to come back again. Thank you to all the staff.

name: Washington R&B Hotel Kyoto Shijo Kawaramachi
detail: I stayed at the hotel during Golden Week. The room was compact, typical of a business hotel, but it was quiet, clean, and the bathtub was spacious, allowing me to relax. There was a coin laundry on the 2nd floor with free detergent and fabric softener, which was helpful. Free coffee was available all day long. The location is convenient, just a short walk from the Shijo Kawaramachi intersection. Behind the hotel, there's a stylish dining area on Kiyamachi Street, and the Kamo River runs nearby, making it pleasant for a walk. The breakfast buffet also had a good value. The staff was very kind, and the cleaning staff greeted me with a Good morning when they passed me in the hallway, which felt nice. I think it's the best hotel in terms of cost-performance.

name: KANSEI Kyoto Hachijo
detail: The price was reasonable, and it was within walking distance from Kyoto Station. The room was also clean. It was nice that check-out was at 11 o'clock. Additionally, both during check-in and check-out, the staff at the front desk were wonderful, and I was able to have a pleasant stay. I would like to stay here again when I go to Kyoto.

name: APA Hotel Kyoto-Eki-Horikawadori
detail: There are several APA Hotels around Kyoto Station, but I chose this one because it had the lowest price in my online search. As expected from an APA Hotel, the single room is small, but since I’m traveling alone, it’s more than enough. The room is well-equipped, and having a large public bath is also a nice bonus. After checking in, I enjoyed dinner at Porta after sightseeing at Kyoto Tower. It’s great that it takes less than 10 minutes to walk to the station. There’s also a convenience store nearby. The dish in the photo is from the breakfast buffet. In addition to this, there was a good selection of bread, juice, and more. I recommend this place if you're looking for a casual stay around the station.

name: APA Hotel Kyoto Ekihigashi
detail: First of all, it’s really just a short distance from the station, and it's very easy to pick up my carry-on case after checking it in. Also, the bath wasn't that crowded, and the building is new and clean. The breakfast is really delicious! There are many kinds of tsukudani, and the flavor of the miso soup was good too. In the kitchen, there seemed to be experienced housewives who were attentive to the seasoning, the layout of the buffet, and any spills, making sure everything was kept clean. I definitely want to stay here again when I visit Kyoto! Thank you very much!
